WhatsApp has launched a user name reservation system a few days ago, and is now beginning to enable full functionality for some users. Details are as follows.

WhatsApp begins activating reserved usernames

Last month, WhatsApp launched a username reservation system, allowing users to claim their exclusive usernames in advance before the full functionality is officially launched.

Users can go to "Settings" > "Account" > "Username" to claim a username, and may choose to allow anyone who knows their username to contact them, or require new contacts to enter an additional four-digit PIN code after inputting the username.

When a chosen username is the same as an account already established on another Meta platform (such as Facebook or Instagram), the user may be required to prove control of the corresponding account. This measure aims to curb the misuse of well-known usernames and potential impersonation scams.

That said, according to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now beginning to activate reserved usernames for a small number of accounts.

Users included in this initial rollout can now see a banner notification at the top of their chat list, informing them that their username has been activated and can be shared with new contacts.

The report states that this feature is being rolled out to both beta users and users of the official WhatsApp version, but emphasises that it currently appears to be limited to a "very small number of users".

To check whether your account has access to this feature, you can look at the banner notification at the top of your chat list, or go to the "Username" section in your profile settings. That section will inform you whether your username has been activated, or display a message such as "Username coming soon — you'll be notified when it's ready".
